_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 10 Mathematical Literacy P1, November 2018 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Mathematical
Literacy questions hang off shared scenario boxes: the scenario (tables, graphs, plans and maps
described in bracketed words) is the 'context' of the first sub-question of each block and applies
to the sub-questions after it. memo_answer gives the guideline's working and final answer with
decimal commas kept; the guideline's mark codes (M method, A accuracy, CA consistent accuracy, RT
reading from table, C conclusion, O opinion, S simplification, R rounding) and level tags are left out.
FORMAT: 75 marks, 1½ hours, five compulsory questions (Q1 15, Q2 21, Q3 15, Q4 8, Q5 16). An official
ERRATA sheet issued after the paper is tracked as paper1_errata.pdf; its amendment to 3.1.3 is recorded

subject: Mathematical Literacy

questions.context: QUESTION 1 | 1.1 Decoform furniture factory shop is having a birthday sale. Mr Dlamini wants to buy a TV plasma unit to the value of R499,00 using the cash option. All prices are value added tax (VAT) inclusive. Study the payment options in TABLE 1 below and answer the questions that follow. [TABLE 1: PAYMENT OPTIONS. CASH OPTION: Television plasma unit (120 cm); price R499,00; discount 10%; VAT inclusive. LAY-BYE OPTION: Television plasma unit (120 cm); price R499,00; deposit 15%; 6 equal monthly instalments; VAT 15%. NB: No discount on lay-bye items.]
questions.text: Write down the cash price.
questions.topic: Finance: VAT, discount and simple interest

questions.text: Calculate the total cost price for the TV plasma unit (cash option).
questions.topic: Finance: VAT, discount and simple interest

questions.text: Determine the original price of the TV plasma unit before VAT was added. Give your final answer to the nearest whole number.
questions.topic: Finance: VAT, discount and simple interest

questions.text: Calculate the deposit amount for the lay-bye option.
questions.topic: Finance: VAT, discount and simple interest

questions.text: Write down the length size of the television plasma unit in metres.
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area and volume

questions.text: Explain the term discrete data.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data
questions.memo_answer: Discrete data is usually whole values, collected by counting people or objects. (Accept any relevant explanation.)

questions.text: The numeric scale for a kitchen plan is given as 1 : 100. Explain what the scale 1 : 100 means.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale, floor plans and elevation plans
questions.memo_answer: Every 1 unit on the plan is equivalent to 100 units in real life. (Accept any relevant explanation.)

questions.context: QUESTION 2 | 2.1 Study TABLE 2 below regarding the increase in the petrol price and answer the questions that follow. [TABLE 2: UNLEADED PETROL (COAST) PRICE PER LITRE, 2018: 3 January R13,93; 7 February R13,63; 7 March R13,27; 4 April R13,89; 2 May R14,38; 6 June R15,20; 4 July R15,43.] [Source: www.sapia.org.za]
questions.text: Write down the price of petrol on 7 March 2018.
questions.topic: Numbers: percentage calculations

questions.text: Calculate the percentage change in the price of petrol between 7 March and 4 April 2018. Use the formula: % change = (new price - old price) ÷ old price x 100%
questions.topic: Numbers: percentage calculations

questions.context: 2.2 Lerato sees that Vodolite has a new price plan for prepaid phones only, available until 30 November 2018. The rates applicable to this price plan are set out in TABLE 3 below. She likes the plan and decides to sign up. [TABLE 3: USAGE - COST. Local call (any network, any time) 90 cents per minute (billed per second); SMS 80 cents per SMS all day; MMS (300 KB or less) R1,20 per MMS; International SMS R1,95 per SMS all day.]
questions.text: During the month of November, Lerato sends one SMS per day to relatives. Calculate how much this activity costs her in rands.
questions.topic: Patterns and relationships: tariff tables and graphs

questions.text: Lerato spends 2 hours 30 minutes talking to her relatives during the month. Calculate how much this costs her. (Assume that there are 30 days in the month.)
questions.topic: Patterns and relationships: tariff tables and graphs
questions.memo_answer:
Time = 2 x 60 + 30 = 150 minutes
Cost = 150 x R0,90 = R135,00

questions.text: Calculate Lerato’s daily cellphone cost for calls in rands.
questions.topic: Patterns and relationships: tariff tables and graphs
questions.memo_answer: Cost per day = R135,00 ÷ 30 = R4,50 per day

questions.text: Mandy and Joshua work together on Market Day at their school. They split their profit according to the ratio 2 : 3 respectively. They make a profit of R500. Calculate the amount Mandy will receive.
questions.topic: Numbers: ratio, rate and proportion
questions.memo_answer:
Parts: 2 + 3 = 5
Mandy will receive 2/5 x R500 = R200

questions.context: 2.4 Lerato is planning to go on holiday in a minibus. She estimates that petrol will cost her R800 to get to her destination. The graph below outlines the relationship between the amount of money that Lerato will have to pay for petrol, and the number of people travelling in the minibus. [Graph NUMBER OF PEOPLE VS PETROL COST: x-axis number of people in the minibus (0-9), y-axis Lerato's petrol cost (0-900); a decreasing curve through the marked points (1; 800), (2; 400), (4; 200) and (8; 100).]
questions.text: Determine how much it will cost Lerato if 4 people travel with her in the minibus.

questions.text: Determine the number of people travelling with her in the minibus, if Lerato uses R400 for her petrol.
questions.topic: Patterns and relationships: tariff tables and graphs

questions.topic: Patterns and relationships: tariff tables and graphs

questions.context: QUESTION 3 | 3.1 Lerato invites her relatives to spend a weekend at her home. She decides to make pancakes for breakfast. The following recipe serves 10 persons. Lerato would like to serve 15 persons. PANCAKES - ingredients: 0,25 kg cake flour; 2 eggs; 500 mℓ water; 5 mℓ salt.
questions.text: Write down, in the simplest form, the number of people the recipe serves as a ratio to the number of people Lerato would like to serve.
questions.topic: Numbers: ratio, rate and proportion

questions.text: How much salt and water does Lerato need to make pancakes for 15 people?
questions.topic: Numbers: ratio, rate and proportion
questions.memo_answer:
Water: 1,5 x 500 mℓ = 750 mℓ
Salt: 1,5 x 5 mℓ = 7,5 mℓ

questions.text: Determine the amount (in grams) of cake flour Lerato will need to make pancakes for 15 people.
questions.topic: Numbers: ratio, rate and proportion
questions.memo_note: The guideline converts the recipe amount (for 10 people) only. The official errata (12 Nov 2018) corrects this to 15 people: 250 x 1,5 = 375 grams (OR 0,25 x 1 000 x 1,5 = 375 g, OR by proportion 15 x 0,25 ÷ 10 = 0,375 kg = 375 g).

questions.text: Allison is feeling creative. She is going to divide a patch of ground into a sandpit for her children to play in, and a flower bed which will look pretty. The patch of ground is 6,5 m wide and 4,5 m long from front to back. She needs to fence the whole area off to prevent the dogs from digging it up. She will leave a 40 cm border on all sides. Calculate in metres length of fencing she needs to enclose the entire perimeter. You may use the following formula: Perimeter = 2 × 𝑙𝑒𝑛𝑔𝑡ℎ + 2 × 𝑏𝑟𝑒𝑎𝑑𝑡ℎ
questions.topic: Measurement: perimeter, area and volume

questions.context: 3.3 Study the thermometer below and answer the questions. [Picture of a thermometer with a Fahrenheit scale (-40 to 120 °F) on the left and a Celsius scale (-40 to 50 °C) on the right.] [Source: holdthesulfites.com]
questions.text: If a patient’s temperature reading is 32 ºC, write down what you estimate that the temperature will be in degrees Fahrenheit.
questions.topic: Measurement: substitution into formulae

questions.text: Show your accuracy by using the following formula to calculate the exact temperature. Round off the final answer to the nearest whole number. °F = 9/5 x °C + 32°
questions.topic: Measurement: substitution into formulae

questions.text: The distance between Kuils River and Beaufort West is 15 cm on a map. Determine the real distance (in km) between the two towns if the scale on the map is 1 : 3 750 000.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale and maps

questions.text: A tin of Nestlé coffee has a diameter of 100 mm and a height of 120 mm. A cardboard box is 500 mm long, 300 mm wide and 240 mm high. [Pictures: a cylindrical coffee tin (diameter 100 mm, height 120 mm) and a rectangular cardboard box (length 500 mm, width 300 mm, height 240 mm).] Determine the maximum number of tins that can be packed in the cardboard box.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: assembly diagrams and packaging models
questions.memo_answer:
Length: 500 mm ÷ 100 mm = 5 tins
Width: 300 mm ÷ 100 mm = 3 tins
Height: 240 mm ÷ 120 mm = 2 tins
Total = 5 x 3 x 2 = 30 tins

questions.context: QUESTION 5 | 5.1 The body mass (in kg) for each member of the under-17 rugby team from Fundakahle High School is recorded in the table below: 47, 55, 53, 58, 51, 60, 58, 46, 55, 44, 55, 50, 62, 49, 52, 64.
questions.text: Write down the mode for the U-17 rugby team.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data

questions.text: Define the term mean.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data
questions.memo_answer: The mean is a type of average obtained when all the scores are added together and then divided by the number of scores. (Accept any relevant explanation.)

questions.text: Calculate the median for the U-17 rugby team.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data

questions.text: Determine the range of body mass for U-17 rugby team.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data

questions.text: A survey was done at Fundakahle High School to determine the number of boys and girls who actually enjoy reading. The results are provided in TABLE 6 below. [TABLE 6: SURVEY RESULTS. Columns: Enjoy reading | Do not enjoy reading | TOTAL. Boys: A | 212 | 327; Girls: 372 | 101 | 473; TOTAL: 487 | B | 800.] Determine the missing values A and B in the table above.
